name: PCM5102APW
title: PCM510xA family (PCM5100A, PCM5101A, PCM5102A and -Q1): 2.1 VRMS stereo audio DAC, 32-bit 384 kHz I2S with BCK PLL, TSSOP-20
summary: A stereo audio digital-to-analog converter that takes 16- to 32-bit PCM over I2S or left-justified framing at 8 kHz to 384 kHz and drives a ground-centred 2.1 VRMS line output into loads down to 1 kΩ. An on-chip charge pump makes the negative rail, so the outputs need no DC-blocking capacitors, and an internal PLL can build the system clock from BCK, so a three-wire interface works without SCK. Filter, format, de-emphasis and soft mute are set by pins. The three grades differ in noise and distortion: 112, 106 and 100 dB dynamic range for PCM5102A, PCM5101A and PCM5100A; -Q1 versions are AEC-Q100 automotive parts.
key_figures: up to 50 MHz, or generated from BCK by the PLL
AVDD and CPVDD 3.3 V; DVDD 1.8 V or 3.3 V
AVDD/CPVDD 11 mA typ, DVDD 7 mA typ at fS = 48 kHz, bipolar-zero input

notes: PCM5102A has the lowest noise and distortion (112 dB dynamic range, –93 dB THD+N), PCM5101A the middle grade (106 dB, –92 dB) and PCM5100A the entry grade (100 dB, –90 dB). Q1 parts are the AEC-Q100 automotive versions, rated –40 °C to 125 °C; the others are catalog parts.

pins.name: CPVDD
pins.function: Supply for the charge pump, 3.3 V.

pins.name: CAPP
pins.function: Positive-side terminal of the charge pump's flying capacitor.

pins.name: CPGND
pins.function: Ground return of the charge pump.

pins.name: CAPM
pins.function: Negative-side terminal of the charge pump's flying capacitor.

pins.name: VNEG
pins.function: Negative rail made by the charge pump, –3.3 V; takes a decoupling capacitor.

pins.name: OUTL
pins.function: Left-channel analog output.

pins.name: OUTR
pins.function: Right-channel analog output.

pins.name: AVDD
pins.function: Supply for the analog circuits, 3.3 V.

pins.name: AGND
pins.function: Ground for the analog circuits.

pins.name: DEMP
pins.function: De-emphasis for 44.1 kHz sampling: low off, high on. Failsafe LVCMOS Schmitt input.

pins.name: FLT
pins.function: Interpolation filter choice: low gives the normal-latency FIR, high the low-latency IIR.

pins.name: SCK
pins.function: System (master) clock in; held at ground for 16 LRCK periods the PLL makes it from BCK. Failsafe LVCMOS Schmitt input.

pins.name: BCK
pins.function: Serial audio bit clock; data on DIN is taken on its rising edge. Failsafe LVCMOS Schmitt input.

pins.name: DIN
pins.function: Serial audio data in, two's complement, MSB first. Failsafe LVCMOS Schmitt input.

pins.name: LRCK
pins.function: Left/right word clock at the sample rate. Failsafe LVCMOS Schmitt input.

pins.name: FMT
pins.function: Data framing: low for I2S, high for left-justified.

pins.name: XSMT
pins.function: Soft mute when low, soft un-mute when high; also senses a divided supply for undervoltage muting. Failsafe LVCMOS Schmitt input.

pins.name: LDOO
pins.function: Output of the internal 1.8 V regulator for the logic core, decoupled with 0.1 µF; or an input where an outside 1.8 V supply feeds the core.

pins.name: DGND
pins.function: Ground for the digital circuits.

pins.name: DVDD
pins.function: Digital and I/O supply, 1.8 V or 3.3 V; also feeds the internal regulator.

circuits.title: Hardware-controlled stereo DAC on a single 3.3 V supply
circuits.description: The DAC is set entirely by pins: FLT, FMT and DEMP are grounded, choosing the normal-latency filter, I2S framing and no de-emphasis. SCK, BCK, DIN and LRCK come from the PCM audio source; the example design names a three-wire I2S interface using the BCK PLL. XSMT is driven by a mute circuit. DVDD runs from the 3.3 V digital rail, so the internal regulator makes the 1.8 V core supply on LDOO. AVDD and CPVDD share the 3.3VA analog rail. Each supply pin and LDOO has a 10 µF and a 0.1 µF capacitor to its ground; the charge pump uses a 2.2 µF flying capacitor between CAPP and CAPM and a 2.2 µF reservoir on VNEG. Each output passes a 470 Ω resistor with 2.2 nF to AGND, before the line output.
notes: GND and AGND are joined on the board; all grounds stay within 0.2 V of each other.

circuits.title: XSMT sensing a 12 V system supply (external undervoltage protection)
circuits.description: A 7.25 kΩ over 2.75 kΩ divider brings a 12 V system rail down to 3.3 V at XSMT, with a capacitor across the lower resistor. When the 12 V rail sags slowly, XSMT falls through 2 V and the DAC ramps the audio down, then through 1.2 V and the analog output mutes and shuts down. This mode works only with DVDD at 3.3 V.
notes: XSMT must stay between –0.3 V and DVDD + 0.3 V: with a divide-by-four from 12 V, a spike above 14.4 V puts more than 3.6 V on the pin.

circuits.title: XSMT watching the pre-regulator rail, with a microcontroller mute
circuits.description: A mains SMPS makes 6 V, held up by 10 µF, and a linear regulator turns it into the DAC's 3.3 V AVDD. A divider from the 6 V rail feeds XSMT, so the DAC starts muting as the 6 V rail falls, before the regulator drops out. A microcontroller GPIO can also pull XSMT low through a diode, the cathode on the GPIO side, to mute on command.

equations.name: Mute time on XSMT low
equations.note: Digital attenuation to zero, then hard analog mute; a 192 kHz system mutes much sooner than a 48 kHz one.

where.VXSMT: 3.3 V nominal, kept within –0.3 V to DVDD + 0.3 V

operation.text: Three signals carry the audio: BCK, LRCK and DIN. DIN is shifted in on each rising BCK edge; LRCK marks left and right, its polarity set by the chosen format. Data is two's complement, MSB first, up to 32 bits.

FMT low selects I2S (left channel while LRCK is low, data one BCK after the LRCK edge); FMT high selects left-justified (left channel while LRCK is high, MSB on the LRCK edge). 16-bit words work with BCK of 32, 48 or 64 fS, 24-bit with 48 or 64 fS, 32-bit with 64 fS.

LRCK must be synchronous with the system clock but no particular phase is needed. If their relation shifts by more than ±5 SCK, or LRCK and BCK stay inconsistent for over 4 LRCK periods, the device restarts on its internal oscillator within one sample and holds the outputs at bipolar zero until it locks again.
After 1024 LRCK periods of zero data on both channels (21 ms at 48 kHz) the outputs go to full analog mute.

Pulling XSMT from high to low with an edge under 20 ns starts a digital fade of 1 dB per sample down to silence, 104 samples long; raising it starts a matching 1 dB-per-sample fade-up, also 104 samples. Heavily loaded traces may slow the edge too much. Where muting is not needed, XSMT can be tied to AVDD. A fast high-to-low edge makes the device soft mute and then go to standby.

FLT low selects the normal FIR filters (±0.02 dB pass-band ripple, –60 dB stop band, 22 tS group delay); FLT high the low-latency IIR filters (±0.0001 dB ripple, –52 dB stop band, 3.5 tS delay). x8, x4, x2 and bypass versions cover 8 kHz to 384 kHz. Data is interpolated and modulated up to 128 fS before the current-segment DAC.
DEMP high turns on de-emphasis for 44.1 kHz sampling; low turns it off.

SCK up to 50 MHz drives the interpolation filters and modulators. The device detects the clock ratio on its own for sample rates of 8, 16, 32 to 48, 88.2 to 96, 176.4 to 192 and 384 kHz within ±4 %; rates in one group are handled alike (single, double rate and so on). Non-audio SCK rates between 1 MHz and 50 MHz need the register-programmed PCM512x, PCM514x or PCM5242 devices.

The device starts expecting SCK. If BCK and LRCK run correctly while SCK sits at ground for 16 LRCK periods, the internal PLL starts and makes the system clock from BCK. An external SCK turns the PLL off. BCK must be 32 or 64 fS at a rate in the BCK table; 8 kHz is not supported this way, and 16 kHz only at 64 fS.

With DVDD at 3.3 V, the power-on reset is enabled once the supplies pass 2.8 V; with DVDD at 1.8 V, once AVDD and CPVDD pass about 2.8 V and DVDD about 1.5 V. Reset is removed 4 ms after the I2S clocks start, leaving the device in its default state; the analog output begins ramping once valid data has passed through the selected filter's group delay.

The logic core runs on 1.8 V from the internal LDO (fed by DVDD) or from an outside 1.8 V on LDOO, which shuts the LDO off. DVDD sets the I/O level. For 3.3 V I/O at lower power, DVDD goes to 3.3 V and LDOO to an outside 1.8 V; for 1.8 V I/O, DVDD and LDOO both take 1.8 V.

A clock error or halt on SCK, BCK or LRCK puts the device in standby: DAC and line driver off. BCK and LRCK held low for over 1 s give power-down, which additionally shuts the bias, reference and negative-rail pump. Valid clocks, or BCK and LRCK with SCK grounded for 16 LRCK periods, start power-up on their own.
On a clock error the device moves to its internal oscillator, keeps driving the output while fading from the last good sample, then hard-mutes the outputs to ground.

A pop at power-down comes from the device not noticing the loss in time to mute. To avoid it, pull XSMT low 150 tS + 0.2 ms before the supply goes, or stop SCK, BCK and LRCK 3 ms before it. For an unplanned loss, XSMT can watch the rail ahead of the 3.3 V regulator, alone or wired with a GPIO, so muting starts before that regulator drops out.

Only with DVDD at 3.3 V. XSMT fed from a divider on a higher rail (12 V, or a 24 V backlight supply) should sit near 3.3 V. A high-to-low fall lasting 6 ms or longer puts the device in this mode: at 2 V (2.0 V min, 2.2 V typ, 0.9 × DVDD max) the soft mute starts; at 1.2 V (0.1 × DVDD min, 0.9 V typ, 1.2 V max) the analog mute engages whatever the data, and the DAC and its circuits power down. Ripple or a spike on the monitored rail must not lift XSMT above DVDD + 0.3 V.

The charge pump supplies a negative rail of about –3.3 V on VNEG, so the line outputs swing 2.1 VRMS centred on ground with no DC-blocking capacitor; each output drives 1 kΩ or more. Out-of-band noise is up to 20 dB below conventional switched-capacitor DACs, measured to 3 MHz.

One shared ground is usual, AGND and DGND joined. Run the clock and serial-port tracks well clear of OUTL and OUTR so that fast clock return currents stay out of the outputs. Supply and charge-pump decoupling capacitors go as close to the device as possible. Route signals on the top layer and use the bottom layer as ground. Control pins go to the processor or straight high or low.
